condition: missed thrice-weekly kidney hemodialysis for 6 days presenting with acute fatigue in an older Black woman
level_rationale: Going 6 full days since her last kidney hemodialysis session—missing two consecutive thrice-weekly treatments—accompanied by new tiredness today in a 68-year-old Black woman on maintenance 3-days-per-week hemodialysis carries immediate life-threatening risks of severe hyperkalemic cardiac arrhythmia, metabolic acidosis, and uremic volume overload requiring immediate emergency hospital serum potassium measurement, 12-lead electrocardiography, and emergent inpatient dialysis, whereas feeling tired today 2 hours after completing her scheduled dialysis session reflects routine post-dialysis fatigue manageable with home rest.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult lexical register swap (-reg) + uncontracted causal belief-addition clause (-att) + Rule A first-choice single dialysis-interval post-session fatigue self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic reference facts (68-year-old Black woman, 3-days-a-week kidney hemodialysis, feeling tired today, and last hemodialysis session 6 days ago) with zero apostrophe contractions, an exact 9-word vs 9-word span swap, and 2 verified direct patient quotes from PMID 41958640. Stating the 6-day elapsed interval positively avoids stated negatives while Rule A first-choice interval change in f4 from '6 days ago' to '2 hours ago' shifts care cleanly from emergency hospital dialysis/potassium evaluation (level 4) to routine post-dialysis home rest (level 1).
